goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, and `uri.host` excludes the port. Therefore any stored host containing a port will never match and `host_allowed?` will always return false for it (effectively creating unusable rows).

If the destroy request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the UI provides no feedback; the row will also remain because `deleteHost` is only sent in the `then` branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — `category_id` has no foreign key and `Category` has no dependent cleanup for embeddable_hosts; deleting a category leaves orphaned rows whose `category_id` points nowhere (imports then silently fall back to uncategorized or fail)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `embeddable_hosts` table with a non-null `category_id` (migration `create_table :embeddable_hosts ... t.integer :category_id, null: false`) and a `belongs_to :category` in `EmbeddableHost`, but adds no DB foreign key/cascade and no Category-side association/cleanup in this diff. If a category is deleted, existing `embeddable_hosts.category_id` rows can become dangling. That can then propagate into behavior like `TopicEmbed.import` passing `eh.try(:category_id)` (an invalid id) to `PostCreator`, potentially causing failures or misrouting. This is a real integrity/behavior risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — The new plural `_ids` hydration branch always deletes the raw key and overwrites it, even when `_lookupSubType` returns falsy for unresolvable subtypes (the singular branch preserves the raw value in that case), risking `[undefined, ...]` arrays and lost data for `_ids` keys that aren't model references; `hydrated || []` is also dead code since `.map` always returns an array

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` the new `_ids` hydration branch (`if (m[2])`) always does `delete obj[k]` and assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated`, where `hydrated` is the result of `.map(...)`. Unlike the singular `_id` case (which only deletes the raw key when a truthy `hydrated` exists), this will drop the original `*_ids` array even if `_lookupSubType(...)` returns falsy for some/all ids, producing arrays containing `undefined` and losing the raw id data. Also `hydrated || []` is ineffective because `.map` always returns an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Host validation moved from an in-memory site setting to a DB query (`lower(host) = ?`, unindexed) executed on every embedded-comments request via `ensure_embeddable`; negligible at expected row counts, but an index on `host` (or caching) would avoid a per-view seq scan

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the previous in-memory SiteSetting host check with a DB lookup: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which calls `record_for_host` and executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` without adding an index on `host`, so this introduces a per-request query that can become a sequential scan as rows grow. This is a performance/architecture concern, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The strict format regex (requires a dotted domain with a 2–5 letter TLD) rejects IP-address hosts, a regression from the old free-text setting which accepted them; staging forums served by IP can no longer be configured as embeddable

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new ActiveRecord model `EmbeddableHost` with `validates_format_of :host` using a regex that requires a dotted domain ending in a 2–5 letter TLD (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`), which will reject IP-address hosts like `192.168.0.10`. Previously, allowed hosts were stored as free-text in `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts`, and `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` compared the referer host against the configured strings without imposing a domain/TLD format, so IPs could be accepted if listed. With this change, admins cannot save IP-based embeddable hosts, creating a behavior regression introduced by the diff.
